prior_defects_status.evidence: session_end_fallback.rs:117-123 (cache store), 195-199 (cache read); failure_monitor.rs:96-104 (new field session_last_known_driving_seconds)
prior_defects_status.note: Only driving_seconds cached from live-session poll. total_laps and best_lap_ms remain hardcoded 0/None because BillingSessionInfo lacks them. Customer sees correct driving time but 0 laps in synth summary. DESIGN-SPEC step 8 acknowledged this as follow-up.

new_defects_found.description: session_last_known_driving_seconds cache is NOT reset by reset_fms_for_session_end. When a session ends and a new session starts, the old session's cached driving_seconds persists and could be used for the new session's synth if the new session ends before being seen live.
new_defects_found.exploit_or_trigger: Session A ends with cached driving_seconds=1000. Session B starts and ends quickly (before any live poll). fetch_and_reconcile synth for session B uses cached 1000 seconds instead of 0.
new_defects_found.suggested_fix: Add session_last_known_driving_seconds: None to reset_fms_for_session_end helper. Ensure cache is cleared on session end.

new_defects_found.description: driver_name in synth branch always empty. Code calls find_my_server_session (which returns None because session is missing) then unwrap_or_default(). No fallback to cached driver_name from monitor.session_last_known_driver as DESIGN-SPEC step 8 required.
new_defects_found.exploit_or_trigger: Any synth trigger: driver_name will be empty string in summary card, even if the driver name was known from prior WS events.
new_defects_found.suggested_fix: Add session_last_known_driver: Option<String> to FailureMonitorState, populate from WS events, fallback in synth branch: .or_else(|| monitor.session_last_known_driver.clone()).

new_defects_found.description: No test coverage for timeout error paths (send-stage timeout, body-read timeout). The bytes_then_from_slice tests cover parse success/failure but not the tokio::time::timeout branches that are critical for V-A fix validation.
new_defects_found.exploit_or_trigger: Regression in timeout handling would go undetected by test suite. Could silently re-introduce V-A class.
new_defects_found.suggested_fix: Add unit tests with mock reqwest::Client that simulates: (a) send timeout, (b) body read stall exceeding BYTES_READ_TIMEOUT. Verify no synth and correct log levels.

new_defects_found.description: Cache update uses send_modify which is eventually consistent. If a synth fires immediately after a live poll in the same tick, the cache might not be visible yet. However, the borrow in the synth branch (line 195) happens after the send_modify in the live branch (line 117) within the same function call, so the watch channel should propagate. Low risk but worth noting.
new_defects_found.exploit_or_trigger: Theoretical race if the watch channel receiver hasn't processed the send_modify before the borrow in the synth branch. Unlikely in practice.
new_defects_found.suggested_fix: None needed — watch channel guarantees latest value on next borrow. Document the assumption.

adversarial_summary: The fix commit 49eb2821 successfully addresses V-A (timeout race) and V-B (client reuse) at their root causes with clean implementations. V-C (synth zeros) is partially addressed: driving_seconds is now cached from live-session polls, but total_laps and best_lap_ms remain hardcoded zeros due to server contract limitations (tracked as follow-up). Two new defects were introduced: W-1 (P1) is a cache cross-session contamination bug where the driving_seconds cache is not reset on session end, risking stale values in subsequent sessions; W-2 (P2) is a regression in driver_name handling where the synth branch always produces an empty driver name instead of falling back to a cached value. Test coverage for the critical timeout paths (V-A fix) is missing. With W-1 fixed, the code reaches CONDITIONAL_PASS at 4.0 — deploy is unblocked but W-2 and W-3 should be addressed in the same commit cycle.
